label: D2 after choosing a2 and landing in S1 (rare a2->S1 transition)
explanation: Fires only at D2, and almost only when the state input is S1 while the last-action input is a2, i.e. a rare transition after choosing a2 (99.3% of activation mass). Never fires at D1 or GO, on S2, or after a1->S1 (common). Uses only inputs observed at D2. Precision is lost mainly in the first ~10 trials of an episode, where the feature is mostly silent (adding ep_trial >= 10 raises dev F1 from 0.92 to 0.94); the low-activation misses are scattered. In the example windows the largest activations (near max) come on a2->S1 rare trials whose D1 showed no reward, and a rare a2->S1 that directly follows another one is somewhat weaker (~0.8 of max); this comes from the examples only and was not checked quantitatively. Active cells have a strongly negative policy logit (favoring a2), consistent with an agent that mostly picks a2.

issues: All factual claims check out on the test split. The feature never fires at D1 or GO (phase != D2 gives recall 0). It never fires when state == S2 (recall 0). The common a1->S1 case covers only 0.7% of activation mass (precision 0.010). The base predicate scores P 0.852, R 0.973, F1 0.909 and mass recall 0.993, matching the reported numbers.

There is one systematic false-positive class, and the explanation already discloses it: the feature is silent early in each episode. On a2->S1 steps with ep_trial < 5 precision is 0.0 (1241 predicted steps); with ep_trial < 10 it is 0.07. Adding ep_trial >= 10 raises test F1 to 0.936 (P 0.907, R 0.968). This is a warm-up effect, not a different meaning.

There is a minor modulation by the hidden good state. Precision is 0.80 on a2->S1 steps when S1 is good and 0.95 when S2 is good. Most activations fall where S2 is good, i.e. where the a2 choice is correct but the transition brought the agent to the bad state. This is graded, not a counterexample class.

The explanation's claim about a repeated rare a2->S1 is only partly testable here. Precision is higher (0.94) when the previous trial was also a rare a2 trial, so the feature does not go silent in that case. Any weakening is in magnitude only, which this tool does not score.
The remaining misses (0.7% of mass) are scattered weak activations (around 0.04 to 0.25 of max), mostly on common a1->S1 D2 steps.
